title: Federico Valverde, Aurelien Tchouameni fined €500,000 by Real Madrid for dressing-room fight
content:
Real Madrid have fined Federico Valverde and Aurelien Tchouameni €500,000 (£432,100; $588,520) following Thursday’s dressing-room fight.

Madrid said both players appeared at a disciplinary hearing on Friday, showed “total repentance” for what had happened and apologised to one another.

Madrid added the two players had also apologised “to the club, their teammates, the coaching staff and the fans”, and would accept the sanction the club considered appropriate.

“In view of these circumstances, Real Madrid has decided to impose a financial penalty of five hundred thousand euros on each player, thus concluding the corresponding internal procedures,” a club statement read.

The Athletic reported on Thursday that Valverde, 27, and Tchouameni, 26, were involved in a dressing-room fight at the club’s training ground and that sources briefed on the incident, speaking on the condition of anonymity to protect relationships, said Valverde was taken to hospital to undergo assessments after sustaining a head injury during the altercation.

Madrid later confirmed Valverde had suffered a head injury and had been diagnosed with “cranioencephalic traumatism” following tests by the club’s medical department. The statement said Valverde was “in good condition”, but he would be out for 10 to 14 days, per medical protocols.

Madrid said in a statement on Thursday that “disciplinary proceedings” had been opened against Valverde and Tchouameni following the incident, which was the second altercation between the pair following their first on Wednesday, just days before their Clasico match against Barcelona.

Multiple sources confirmed Thursday’s altercation was instigated by a strong tackle from Valverde on Tchouameni in training. After the session had concluded and the squad returned to the dressing room, Tchouameni confronted Valverde and, after a verbal dispute, it became physical.

During the argument, Valverde fell and hit his head on a table in the changing room. He was subsequently taken to hospital to undergo tests and returned home.

The Athletic reported that Kylian Mbappe was involved in an angry flare-up with a member of staff during a training exercise before their 1-1 draw at Real Betis on April 24.

Last month, Antonio Rudiger was involved in a heated argument with a team-mate in the dressing rooms at Madrid’s training ground, which he has since apologised for.
